title: zazz command operations
description: The zazz subcommands. Each is reached as `zazz SUB ...` (the invoker run under the name zazz sends `zazz` first), as `zazzle zazz SUB ...`, or in-process as `zazzled run zazz SUB ...`; an installed shim NAME sends `zazz exec-name NAME ARGS`. Seven are also MCP tools of `zazzled mcp` (zazz_new, zazz_test, zazz_pack, zazz_add, zazz_call, zazz_describe, zazz_ls); keygen, sign, trust, install, run, uninstall, list, rm and doctor are not. Agent-facing commands reply with one JSON value, or `{"error": {"code", "message", ...}}` with exit status 2; pack's own failures are `error: ...` lines; the human commands (run, install, uninstall, list) reply in plain text. help only prints text and is left out.

entities.name: zazz new
entities.description: Creates a Rust script directory to start from.
entities.transport: zazz new NAME; MCP tool zazz_new
entities.authorization: Callers of the daemon's own uid (checked by the socket server); writes NAME/ in the caller's working directory.
entities.result: {dir, files: [zazz.json, src/main.rs, tests/basic.rs], next}: a manifest, a json-command handler that counts lines and words, and tests using zazz::test.
failures: No name or more than one: usage.
A name that is not lowercase letters, digits and '-' or is one of zazz's own words: bad_input.
The directory exists: exists.

entities.name: zazz pack
entities.description: Packs a script directory into a deterministic .zazz.
entities.transport: zazz pack DIR [-o FILE]; MCP tool zazz_pack
entities.authorization: Callers of the daemon's own uid; the output must lie under the working directory or a temp directory.
entities.result: {path, hash: b3:..., name, bytes}; the default output is DIR.zazz beside DIR, written atomically.
failures: No directory: `usage: zazz pack DIR [-o FILE]`.
A directory that does not pack (no valid manifest, over the archive limits).
An output outside the working directory or a temp directory: `refusing to write ... outside the working directory or a temp directory`.

entities.name: zazz test
entities.description: Builds a script and runs its tests without registering it.
entities.transport: zazz test DIR|FILE [--update]; MCP tool zazz_test
entities.authorization: Callers of the daemon's own uid; the build and tests run in the OS sandbox with no network but the test replay file.
entities.result: {name, build: "ok", tests: {passed, ignored, failed, duration_ms} or null, warnings}; nothing is published (scratch space is removed). With --update (directories only) snapshots under tests/snapshots are rewritten, which makes it a write.
failures: --update with a .zazz file: usage.
No toolchain or no wasm32-wasip1 target for a Rust script: no_toolchain, saying how to install it.
Compile errors: build_failed with up to 20 condensed diagnostics {level, file, line, col, msg, hint}.
A module zazz-worker refuses: invalid_wasm.
Failing tests: tests_failed with the report.
No OS sandbox: sandbox_unavailable; no zazz-worker: no_worker.
kind native-bin: unsupported.

entities.name: zazz add
entities.description: Builds, tests and registers a .zazz by the hash of its bytes.
entities.transport: zazz add FILE.zazz; MCP tool zazz_add
entities.authorization: Callers of the daemon's own uid; the file is opened without following symlinks and must be a regular file within the archive size limit. A signature is checked, and trust is decided by root-owned anchors or the Keychain, not by the caller.
entities.result: {hash: b3:..., name, status: compiled|cached, runtime: wasm|native, tests, warnings, signer, trusted}; `cached` when the id is registered already. Warnings say when there are no tests, the signer is not trusted here, or native was asked for but not granted.
failures: Not one argument: usage.
Unreadable, a symlink, not a regular file: unreadable; too large or a bad archive: invalid_archive; a bad manifest: invalid_manifest; a bad signature: invalid_signature.
Build and test failures as for zazz test (build_failed, invalid_wasm, tests_failed, no_toolchain, sandbox_unavailable, no_worker, unsupported).
No tests while the root-owned policy sets require_tests: tests_missing.
A script declaring openapi that does not return a document: invalid_openapi, and the script is removed again.
Registry errors: store.

entities.name: zazz call
entities.description: Runs a registered script's json-command, or one service-call operation, in a warm worker.
entities.transport: zazz call ID [JSON|-] or zazz call ID OPERATION [--params JSON] [--body JSON|-]; MCP tool zazz_call (input, or operation with params and body)
entities.authorization: Callers of the daemon's own uid. The script touches only its manifest's paths (relative to the caller's directory, $TMP and $HOME), narrowed by its signer's grants; it gets network only when its signer is trusted with it here and the root-owned policy allows network.
entities.result: The script's output JSON; when it also wrote to captured streams (over MCP), {output, stdout, stderr}. Through the invoker the script reads and writes the caller's own streams (stdin is /dev/null when the input came from `-`).
failures: Bad arguments or input that is not JSON: usage, bad_input.
An unknown id, a prefix shorter than 12 hex digits or matching several scripts: not_found.
No OS sandbox for a WASM worker: sandbox_unavailable; no zazz-worker: no_worker.
The worker fails to start or stops: script_crashed.
The call runs past the manifest's call_ms (plus 5 s): timeout; the caller hangs up: cancelled (a cancel is sent, then the worker is killed).
The script's own error result: its error object (codes such as timeout, out_of_memory, network_denied, sandbox_denied from the worker or SDK).

entities.name: zazz ls
entities.authorization: Callers of the daemon's own uid.
entities.result: [{id (b3: and 12 hex digits), name, version, runtime, tests, added_at}], newest first.
failures: Registry errors: store.

entities.name: zazz describe
entities.description: Says what a registered script is, how it runs and what it may touch.
entities.transport: zazz describe ID|PREFIX|NAME; MCP tool zazz_describe
entities.authorization: Callers of the daemon's own uid.
entities.result: {id, name, version, description, runtime, messages, sandbox, cli (whether it has a cli spec), operations (OpenAPI operation ids), tests, signer}.
failures: Not one argument: usage.
An id that resolves to no script: not_found.

entities.name: zazz rm
entities.description: Removes a registered script and every name installed for it.
entities.authorization: Callers of the daemon's own uid.
entities.result: {removed: b3:...}; its modules, native binary, metadata, lock, names and shims are gone.
failures: Not one argument: usage.
An id that resolves to no script: not_found.

entities.name: zazz keygen
entities.description: Makes a signing authority: a P-256 key and a self-signed certificate with the zazz signing purpose and grants.
entities.transport: zazz keygen NAME [--native] [--network none|all|HOST,...] [--read P,...] [--write P,...] [--days N]
entities.authorization: Callers of the daemon's own uid; writes NAME.key (0600, refused if it exists) and NAME.crt in ~/.zazzle/keys (0700).
entities.result: {key, cert, grants, next}: the grants default to no native code and no network; validity defaults to 365 days; next says how to trust it.
failures: A bad option, no name or a bad --days: usage.
A bad name or host pattern: bad_input.
The key exists: exists.

entities.name: zazz sign
entities.description: Signs a .zazz with a key from the keys directory.
entities.authorization: Callers of the daemon's own uid; the output must lie under the working directory or a temp directory.
entities.result: {path, hash, signer}: a copy of the archive with zazz.sig (the digest, an ECDSA P-256 signature and the signer's chain), written to OUT or over FILE; the signed file has a new id.
failures: Bad arguments: usage; several keys and no --key: usage.
No key, or an unreadable key or certificate: no_key.
An unreadable file, bad archive or manifest: unreadable, invalid_archive, invalid_manifest.
An output outside the allowed directories: io.

entities.name: zazz trust
entities.description: Lists, adds and removes the authorities this machine trusts.
entities.transport: zazz trust ls | add CERT | rm NAME
entities.authorization: ls: callers of the daemon's own uid, listing only anchors in a root-owned /etc/zazzle/trust.d. add and rm write that directory, which needs root; on macOS add also sets Keychain trust, for which macOS asks the person to authenticate. Not offered over MCP.
entities.result: ls: [{authority, grants}]; add: {trusted, path} (the certificate as NAME.pem); rm: {removed}.
failures: Anything else: `usage: zazz trust ls | add CERT | rm NAME`.
An unreadable certificate file: io; no certificate in it: bad_input.
No permission to write or remove in the trust directory: permission, suggesting sudo.

entities.name: zazz doctor
entities.authorization: Callers of the daemon's own uid.
entities.result: One check each for rustc, the wasm32-wasip1 target, zazz-worker, the OS sandbox, the registry and the shim directory: ok, or the problem and how to fix it.

entities.name: zazz install
entities.description: Makes a script a command a person can run.
entities.authorization: Callers of the daemon's own uid; writes a name in the registry and a symlink in $ZAZZ_BIN or ~/.zazzle/bin, replacing only an existing symlink.
entities.result: `installed NAME (b3:...) as PATH`, with a reminder to put the shim directory on PATH when it is not; a file is added first (as zazz add).
failures: Bad arguments: exit 2.
An add failure or an unknown id: exit 1 with its code and message.
A name that is invalid or reserved: exit 2.
No invoker beside zazzled, or a non-symlink file where the shim goes: exit 1.

entities.name: zazz run and installed shims
entities.description: Runs a script as a person would: flags parsed from its manifest, plain output.
entities.transport: zazz run NAME|ID [ARGS...]; NAME [ARGS...] through a shim (zazz exec-name NAME ARGS)
entities.result: What the script wrote to the caller's stdout, then its returned output rendered (strings raw, tables on a terminal, JSON otherwise; raw JSON with --json unless the script defines --json); the script's exit code. --help prints the usage generated from the cli spec.
failures: No name: `usage: zazz run NAME|ID [ARGS...]`.
No such script: `NAME: not_found: ...`, exit 127.
Arguments the cli spec rejects: the parser's message, exit 2.
A call failure or the script's error: `NAME: CODE: message`, exit 1 or the script's exit code.

entities.name: zazz uninstall
entities.description: Removes an installed command; the script stays registered.
entities.authorization: Callers of the daemon's own uid; removes the shim only if it is a symlink.
failures: Not one name: usage, exit 2.
A name that is not installed: exit 1.

entities.name: zazz list
entities.authorization: Callers of the daemon's own uid.
entities.result: Installed names with their script ids, one per line.
